<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via DatasourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via DatasourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f85395814eda2185bcd090ace6e633d091ba6d1e` — the merge of head `a2d8e887a81615b456977522e92d664f280bc80d` into base `2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f85395814eda2185bcd090ace6e633d091ba6d1e && git checkout f85395814eda2185bcd090ace6e633d091ba6d1e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486 a2d8e887a81615b456977522e92d664f280bc80d && git checkout -B drift-repro 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486 && git merge --no-ff a2d8e887a81615b456977522e92d664f280bc80d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a2d8e887a81615b456977522e92d664f280bc80d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.test.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.metadata-redaction.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.data-door-stored-metadata-redaction.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-service.test.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-credential-fields.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver-sql.zod.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-redaction.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/declared-datasources.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-plugin.ts

Inputs: card #28633 (body and all 8 comments, including the ruling record 6557788232, claim amendments 6557238812 / 6557268469 and the dev's os-dev-report 6558370233), PR #28674 (body, file list, net diff at `a2d8e887` against `origin/main` — `main` has moved to `2678600d` since the merge base `6b9c1ca9` but touched none of the eight PR files nor any cited module, so the net diff is the eight files), the check-runs on the head, and the live tree read at `origin/main` and `pr28674`.

Check-runs on the head at the time of reading (41): 13 completed success (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, Plan Test Core shards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Flag docs affected, filter), 8 skipped (opt-in and matrix shards), and 20 in_progress: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1–8, Lint · ESLint / docs & code guards / repo & tooling gates / CI, release & engine gates / scoped ×2, Type Check ×4, Live E2E UI. That is an honest reading, not a verdict on those families: the dev's local run of the 80 derived families (80 × exit 0, 0 NOT-MEASURED) and the full dogfood (VERDICT exit 0) are the only measured answers so far, and queue entry still waits on the CI conclusions. Nothing below depends on them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`DatasourceSchema.ssl.key` gains `.meta({ credential: 'value' })`** (`datasource.zod.ts`). A `.meta()` adds no validation: the field stays `z.string().optional()`, the `ssl` block stays `strictObject` with the same five members and the same aliases (`privatekey` / `clientkey` → `key`), so the accept set of the published schema is unchanged and `Metadata-protocol: none` is **right**. The one public-surface effect is the marker itself, read by the derivation (`metadata-credential-fields.ts`) and the ratchet; no exported type moves and no generated spec artifact carries the marker (none on `main` carries webhook's either). **Right.**

2. **`redactDatasourceItem` gains a second half** (`metadata-type-redaction.ts` 123–144): the unchanged `config` rule first, then `derivedCredentialRedactorFor(getMetadataTypeSchema('datasource'))` applied to the already-config-redacted item. The served answer of every exit that resolves the `datasource` redactor loses `ssl.key` when present and names `ssl.key` in `redactedKeys`. Read in the tree, the exits that inherit with no code change are: `/meta` list, item and layered (`protocol.ts` 9674 / 11000 / 12284–12286 through `redactMetadataItem` → `getMetadataTypeRedactor`), `getMetaItemsPerPackage` on the served face (the body of `GET /packages/:id/export`, `runtime/domains/packages.ts` 3230), `diffMetaItem` (28178), the diagnostics face (`metadata-diagnostics.ts` 360), the `sys_metadata` / `sys_metadata_history` data door (`protocol.ts` 14062 / 14224, `runtime/stored-metadata-reader-seam.ts`, `service-automation` crud nodes, the MCP stdio data bridge 843), `MetadataManager.getPublished` (`metadata-manager.ts` 2285–2297), the audit writer and the stored-body migration (`plugin-audit`), and the realtime publish seam (`objectql/engine-realtime-publish.ts` 163). So the brief's list — `/meta` list / item / layered, the data door, `getPublished`, and the export path — is covered by one lookup, and so are three exits the PR body does not list (package export, diff, realtime publish). **Right.**

3. **The execution faces stay raw, and the connect path reads them.** `getMetaItemsForExecution` / `getMetaItemForExecution` and `MetadataManager.get` / `list` apply no redactor; every datasource load on the connect and boot path reads those (`runtime/declared-datasources.ts` 371 `metadata.get('datasource')`, `service-datasource/plugin.ts` 181 and 282, `datasource-admin-plugin.ts` 482 / 487, `external-validation-plugin.ts` 399). A stored key therefore still reaches the driver factory. **Right** — the narrowing is a serving act only, as the module's contract (lines 26–31) requires.

4. **The item-by-reference contract holds**: with nothing to withhold the input object is returned (`return { item, redactedKeys: [] }`), so the data door's "stored bytes reach the caller" control and `redactStoredMetadataBody`'s identity short-circuit keep working. `redactedKeys` is now `.sort()`ed over both halves, which is what the `MetadataRedactionResult` docblock already promises ("sorted"). **Right.**

5. **The ratchet's description rule widens** to `passphrases?` and `private[ _-]?keys?` (`metadata-credential-fields.test.ts` 59). Read against every reachable field: the only newly matched position is `datasource:ssl.key`, now marked. `driver-sql.zod.ts` 68 (`SSLConfigSchema.key`, "Client private key …") sits under `config`, a `z.record`, which the walk does not enter; the postgres and mysql driver configs declare `ssl` as a boolean toggle only (`driver/common.zod.ts` 77) and refuse the certificate-bearing object form inside `config`; `connector-auth.zod.ts` 543–555 (`appPrivateKey`) sits inside the `auth` union, unreachable; mongo's `options` description mentions `passphrase` outside its first sentence and under the config record. So no other registered type reds and no non-datasource type is newly redacted: the derivation acts on markers alone, and the only markers in the tree are webhook's two and this one. **Right.**

6. **Cleared and absent forms**: `key: ''` is served as written and not named (the module's cleared-form rule); an `ssl` block without `key`, or no `ssl` block, is returned by reference. A `key: null` would be withheld and named (`value === undefined || isClearedForm` lets `null` through to the withholding branch); the carry-forward then grafts `null` back, so nothing is lost — an observation, not a defect.

7. **An edit that sends the served item back erases nothing.** `carryForwardRedactedValues` (`metadata-redaction.ts` 486–575) re-runs the redactor on the stored body, walks `redactedKeys`, and grafts the stored `ssl.key` wherever the incoming body still carries the `ssl` container with `key` absent — exactly the served shape. The GET → edit → PUT pin in `protocol.metadata-redaction.test.ts` exercises that path through the real save door. A PUT that omits the whole `ssl` block removes it (author intent, the same posture as `config`), and `key: ''` clears it. **Right.**

8. **The datasource admin door is untouched** (`packages/services/service-datasource` is not in the diff): it reads raw through `metadata.get`, withholds the key with its own `servableSsl` (`datasource-admin-service.ts` 176–181) and carries it forward on edit (958–966), landed by #28648. Its behaviour is unchanged by this PR. See ④ for what that leaves.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28633-datasource-ssl-key-redaction.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the BREAKING banner, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, and the title carries `!`.
- `Clause-②: no` is defined (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` 2182–2184) as "widens no published accept set or public surface; add `(narrowing)` if it narrows". Judged in ①: the diff widens nothing (no new accepted key or value, no new served member, no new export) and narrows one read answer, so `no (narrowing)` is **right**; `yes (narrowing)` was #28648's arm because that PR also added served members, which this one does not.
- Level: AGENTS.md §3 — `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; the level follows the protocol kind alone; `none` takes `patch`; "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". The gate's own self-test names this exact pair (`no (narrowing)` + `none` ⇒ `patch`, `none-clean`). No authorable key, export or config field is removed or renamed, so no migration mapping or tombstone is owed. `Check Changeset` on the head: success. **`patch` is right.**
- Only `@objectstack/spec` publishes a source change; the other five files are tests. No `skip-changeset`. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report 6558370233):

1. *File surface beyond amendment 6557268469* — `datasource.zod.ts` (the marker and its docblock) and `metadata-credential-fields.test.ts` (two words). Both are the order's own preference (derive the set from schema credential markers where the module supports it, and it does), and ruling record 6557788232 already places the `packages/spec` edit with seat 3 under the maintainer's delegation. **Accepted**; the seat amends the claim's file-surface line to name the two files.
2. *Seat note asking for the `ssl` arm in `data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts`, not taken* — **correctly not taken**. That module derives driver-config credentials from each driver's `z.never()` contract plus the alias residue (its header and `refusedCredentialPaths`, 308–366); `ssl` is a sibling of `config`, not a member of it, and the driver configs declare `ssl` as a boolean toggle only. Adding `ssl.key` there would have been the second hand list the card forbids; the marker is the one declaration, and the ratchet makes a dropped marker red (ablation A2 / A3 in the report).
3. *`Fixes #28633`, not `Part of`* — matches the ruling record's condition ("Its PR says `Fixes #28633`"). **Consistent.**
4. / 5. The preflight re-run after committing the consumer tests, and the stopped first build — procedural, no contract effect.

Open question (needs_decision): *should the spec also refuse an authored inline `ssl.key` on `DatasourceSchema`, or keep it accepted and redacted on read?*

**Answered: A, as this PR does — and the refusal is not owed by this card.** Grounds read in the tree, not the PR body: (i) the published spec on `main` declares `ssl.key` as "PEM format or path to file"; the path form carries no secret and is the one way a code-defined datasource reaches mutual TLS today, since no sealed channel or `ssl` key reference is declared and `external.credentialsRef` is the driver-password channel only. A `z.never()` refusal (B) would therefore take a declared, delivered capability away at the consumer with no replacement — the shape ④ forbids outright. (ii) The posture A leaves is exactly the one ruling B+ on #24966 already gives `webhook.secret`: accepted, at rest in the row, withheld on every read exit, carried forward on save. (iii) The admin door's refusal (#28648) is that HTTP door's own posture on a sealed-channel question and binds nothing in spec. (iv) C (a declared secret reference for the client key, then refuse the inline value) is new spec surface with no measured producer: **escalated to the spec lane as a follow-up card, to be opened when a producer needs mTLS through a sealed channel**, not as a condition on this PR. The cost A names — a `/meta`-saved or code-defined row may hold key material at rest — is the pre-existing posture of every credential value the B+ derivation covers and is not widened here.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged over the floor (every non-prose path of the diff, the two schema-face hits first) against the published spec on `main`.

**Does the narrowing take a declared capability away at the consumer?** No. The spec declares `ssl.key` authorable and stored; nothing on `main` reads `ssl.key` from a served exit — every connect-path load goes through the raw faces (① 3). The exits that lose it are serving exits, and for each the spec's own invariant (#8154 / #8300, lines 4–5 and 18–34 of the module: "stored credentials must never serve cleartext") already applies to `config.password`; the diff makes that refusal real for the one `ssl` member that is key material. `ca` and `cert` are public material and stay served, so a reader of the TLS posture loses nothing it can act on. The package export (`GET /packages/:id/export`) now exports a datasource without its key, as it already exports one without `config.password`: the same refusal, not a new one. The narrowing **makes the spec's own refusal real** and retires no declared capability. Holds.

**Trying to break it:**

- *Marker read off the registry, not the schema.* The new half derives from `getMetadataTypeSchema('datasource')`, and `registerMetadataTypeSchema` (`metadata-type-schemas.ts` 343) lets any plugin replace that entry; an override without the marker would serve `ssl.key` again while the `config` half still holds, and nothing would say so. No caller in the tree registers a `datasource` schema (grepped `packages/**` and `ui/**`), and the ratchet guards the spec's own copy, so the exposure is hypothetical today — but it is the fail-open shape the module's own note (lines 192–199) names as "the worst available outcome", and the built-in could read `DatasourceSchema` directly (the sibling registry module already imports it). **Should-fix**, not a FAIL: pin the built-in half to `DatasourceSchema` (or memoise on it) rather than on the overridable registry entry.
- *A second declaration of which `ssl` member is secret.* `datasource-admin-service.ts` 144 (`SSL_PRIVATE_KEY = 'key'`, with `servableSsl` and the edit carry-forward) is a hand-written twin of the marker, landed by #28648 before the marker existed. Both agree today, and the ratchet protects the spec side; the admin side can drift silently if the schema ever marks a second `ssl` member (a passphrase, say). The card's "no second hand list" wanted this for the kept-key set, and the same reasoning applies here. **Should-fix**, follow-up in `service-datasource`: derive that door's withheld set from `credentialFieldsOf(DatasourceSchema)` or apply the spec redactor, so one declaration serves both doors.
- *Memoisation.* `derivedCredentialRedactorFor` caches per schema identity; `DatasourceSchema` is one `lazySchema` proxy for the process, so the walk runs once and the cache cannot go stale against a static marker. Holds.
- *Ordering with `_diagnostics`.* Unchanged: the consumer computes diagnostics on the raw body before redaction, and the redactor still leaves every non-credential key byte-for-byte. Holds.
- *Ratchet widening reds nothing else* (① 5), and ablation A3 in the report shows why the widening is needed (the `main` rule did not read "Client private key" as a credential). Holds.
- *Snapshot and audit surfaces.* `sys_metadata_history` rows, audit-writer snapshots and the stored-body migration all go through `redactStoredMetadataBody` and inherit; pinned for history in the data-door test. Holds.
- *The `(narrowing)` arm's full-dogfood duty* — run by the dev (VERDICT exit 0, 2981 passed) and `Dogfood Regression Gate` completed success on the head. Holds.

Nothing found at must-fix. Two should-fix findings, both follow-ups that do not change what this head serves.

### 核对六项
